item.description: Scaling capacitive pressure sensor arrays to large areas remains challenging due to electrode alignment errors, fabrication complexity, and limited dynamic range inherent in conventional parallel-plate architectures. item.title: Workplace Ageism, Job Satisfaction, and Depressive Symptoms Among Older Workers: The Roles of US-Born Status
item.description: More than 60% of older workers report experiencing ageism in the workplace, yet little is known about whether the relationship between ageism, job satisfaction, and mental health differs by US-born status. This study examined whether job satisfaction mediates the association between workplace ageism and depressive symptoms and assessed whether this association differs by US-born status. Data were drawn from the 2018 and 2020 National Longitudinal Survey of Youth 1979 for workers aged 53- 62, and...

item.description: Yeast platforms are rapidly transitioning from traditional eukaryotic model organisms to versatile, programmable chassis for next-generation human health applications. This review systematically examines the translational evolution of conventional and non-conventional yeasts including Saccharomyces cerevisiae, Komagataella phaffii, Saccharomyces boulardii, and Yarrowia lipolytica and redefines them as scalable biomanufacturing factories and advanced living therapeutics. item.title: SH3YL1-TLR5 complex-mediated vicious cycle contributes to FSGS pathogenesis
item.description: The mechanisms underlying focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS), particularly podocyte damage, remain unclear. We found that patients with FSGS have significantly elevated serum and urine levels of SH3YL1, especially in more severe cases. Adriamycin stimulates SH3YL1 secretion, which induces proinflammatory cytokines and enhances podocyte injury. The receptor for secreted SH3YL1 is identified as Toll-like receptor 5 (TLR5), with the ectodomain specifically binding SH3YL1 at an affinity of...

item.title: Clinicians' confidence in synthetic neuroimaging: a survey from the EANS emerging Technologies and Innovations in Neurosurgery (ETIN) taskforce
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Neurosurgery relies heavily on imaging for diagnostic, planning, intra-operative decision-making, and image-guided interventions. Machine learning (ML) enables synthetic imaging, such as synthetic CT (sCT) generated from MRI or biplanar X-rays, potentially reducing radiation exposure and improving imaging access. However, clinicians' confidence in synthetic imaging remains poorly understood.

item.description: Rosa rugosa root extract (RR-r) has been used in East Asian medicine to treat metabolic disorders, including diabetes and alcohol-induced liver toxicity. item.title: Multi-omics perspectives on mitochondrial vulnerability in the aging liver: biological modules and translational implications
item.description: Chronological age alone is an incomplete proxy for the biological heterogeneity of the aging liver. Mitochondrial vulnerability may provide a mechanistic link between biological aging and the loss of hepatic resilience under metabolic, toxic, and ischemic stress. Accumulating multi-omics evidence suggests that hepatic aging is best understood as a set of coordinated pathway-level disturbances rather than through isolated biomarkers. Transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic studies converge on...

item.title: Clinicopathologic characteristics and molecular landscape for pseudomyxoma peritonei of appendiceal origin
item.description: Pseudomyxoma peritonei (PMP) of appendiceal origin presents a unique challenge in oncology owing to its rarity, varied progression, and complex molecular characteristics. The current standard treatment using cytoreductive surgery combined with hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy has shown some success in extending survival rates; however, it is associated with significant physical burdens and high recurrence rates. item.title: Cep57 organizes pericentriolar material through dual architectural modules and prevents human mosaic variegated aneuploidy
item.description: Mosaic variegated aneuploidy (MVA) is a developmental disorder associated with chromosome segregation defects. Mutations in the centrosomal protein Cep57 cause MVA2 syndrome, yet the molecular basis of Cep57 function has remained unclear. Here, using MINFLUX nanoscopy, structural biology, biochemical approaches, and analyses of patient-derived cells, we show how Cep57 organizes the inner pericentriolar material (PCM) to support centriole biogenesis. item.title: Family-Supported mHealth Coaching for Middle-Aged Men With Chronic Liver Disease and Metabolic Risk Factors: Protocol for a Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This pilot RCT evaluates an IMB model-informed, family-supported mHealth coaching intervention integrating app-based self-monitoring and individualized coaching. The findings will provide preliminary evidence regarding feasibility, acceptability, and changes in patient- and family-related outcomes and will inform intervention refinement and the design of a future definitive RCT.

item.description: The Asia-Pacific Leukemia Consortium (APLC) working group for Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (APLC ALLWG) recognized the critical need for standardized approaches to measurable residual disease (MRD) assessment and management in adult acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). item.description: Ultraviolet (UV)-induced photodamage drives oxidative stress, DNA damage, and chronic inflammation, leading to progressive cellular ultrastructure and skin function degeneration. item.description: Tin halide perovskites are promising lead-free semiconductors for next-generation electronics; however, their implementation is constrained by a fragile crystal framework, facile Sn^(2+) oxidation, and rapid crystallization kinetics. Here, we establish a molecular design principle for non-metallic thiocyanate (SCN^(-)) additives that stabilizes the formamidinium tin iodide (FASnI(3)) lattice and enables high-performance, stable p-channel thin-film transistors (TFTs). item.title: How early microbial encounters shape adult behavior
item.description: Microbes are increasingly recognized as modulators of host behavior, but the underlying mechanisms are poorly understood. A new PLOS Biology study reveals a microbiome-to-gut-to-neuron pathway linking developmental microbial exposure to later food avoidance.

item.title: Polygenic adaptation signals reveal selection on key behavioral traits early in dog domestication history
item.description: Dogs, the first domesticated animals, show behavioral and morphological changes shaped by artificial selection, but when and where these traits were selected remains unclear. Analyzing two independent canine genomic datasets comprising 1,987 and 722 individuals, we found that polygenic shifts in key behavioral traits associated with domestication were more consistently shared across dog lineages than those in morphological traits. item.title: Evaluations of significant loci associated with mammographic breast density in Korean women
item.description: CONCLUSION: Our findings indicate that mammographic density phenotypes are influenced by a limited number of recurrent loci: 6q25.1, 8p11.23, and 22q13 in Korean women. All three loci identified in this study were previously associated with breast density and breast cancer, validating our findings and suggesting partial genetic overlap between mammographic density and breast cancer risk. item.description: Phospholipase C zeta 1 (PLCZ1), the principal sperm-derived factor, initiates intracellular calcium (Ca²⁺) oscillations at fertilization; however, its contribution to post-fertilization embryonic development remains unclear. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: A composite anatomic model better explains nasal and auricular aging than cartilage atrophy alone. Treatment should address the dominant tissue abnormality, with surgery considered for major structural deformity or functional impairment.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Cancer was associated with a higher incidence of clinically significant pericardial effusion. Among patients with cancer, this phenotype identified a substantially higher risk of death and increased risks of NOAF and HF, and the excess risk was not explained by early periprocedural mortality alone.

item.title: Skin-Protective Effects of Marinophyll, a Carotenoid From Marine Erythrobacter sp. SDW2
item.description: CONCLUSION: Marinophyll demonstrates significant antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and skin barrier-enhancing properties, making it a promising candidate for therapeutic applications in managing oxidative stress and inflammation-associated skin disorders.

item.title: Multimodal imaging features of primary jaw lymphoma: a retrospective analysis of 53 cases
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Primary jaw lymphoma demonstrated characteristic features including severe cortical destruction with micro-perforation and prominent soft-tissue swelling. Frequent cortical micro-perforations highlight the importance of careful CT evaluation for subtle cortical breakthrough. Recognition of these features, particularly with non-specific clinical symptoms, may improve early diagnostic suspicion, reduce misdiagnosis as odontogenic infection, and facilitate timely biopsy and management.

item.title: Greater Glenoid Chondral Lesion Extent and Lack of Labral Coverage Are Associated With the Development of Radiographic Osteoarthritis After Arthroscopic Bankart Repair
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The extent of glenoid chondral lesions and lack of postoperative labral coverage were associated with the development of radiographic osteoarthritis after arthroscopic Bankart repair at a minimum of 2-year follow-up.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Incomplete Pentalogy of Cantrell should be considered in dogs presenting with combined ventral midline defects and peritoneopericardial diaphragmatic hernia. In carefully selected cases, primary reconstruction without prosthetic material may be feasible, but longer follow-up is required. Postoperative cardiovascular reassessment may also aid phenotypic classification when preoperative cardiac assessment is limited by herniated viscera.

item.title: Shedding the Skin: Lamia, Metamorphosis, and Plastic Surgery
item.description: Metamorphosis has long provided artists and writers with a way to explore the relationship between bodily form and identity. In John Keats's Lamia, a serpent undergoes a painful transformation into a woman, shedding her former appearance before recognizing her new human form. John William Waterhouse's paintings of Lamia (1905 and 1909) make this transformation visually tangible through the serpent's discarded skin. item.title: Li-Fraumeni syndrome presenting with early-onset eyelid sebaceous carcinoma
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This is an Asian case of eyelid sebaceous carcinoma associated with genetically confirmed LFS. It expands the tumor spectrum of LFS and highlights the need to consider genetic counseling and testing in young patients presenting with sebaceous carcinoma, particularly when accompanied by multiple primary malignancies or a relevant family history. Early recognition of LFS is essential for personalized management and surveillance of both patients and at-risk relatives.

item.description: Carotid body tumors are rare neuroendocrine neoplasms in dogs, and evidence-based treatment options for malignant or unresectable cases remain poorly defined. item.description: CONCLUSION: In this large prospective real-world cohort, ICI-based therapy significantly improved survival outcomes compared with chemotherapy in advanced NSCLC, particularly in the first-line setting, supporting the effectiveness of immunotherapy-based strategies in routine clinical practice.

item.title: Association between preoperative E/e' and early left ventricular systolic recovery after coronary artery bypass grafting
item.description: CONCLUSION: A higher preoperative E/e' was associated with early improvement in LV systolic function after CABG among patients with a preoperative LVEF of <50% who survived to undergo early postoperative echocardiographic assessment. Given the small number of events and the single-center retrospective design, these findings are hypothesis-generating and require external validation.

item.title: Efficacy of Dual-Wavelength Light-Emitting Diode Phototherapy for Chronic External Otitis: A Randomized Controlled Pilot Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This pilot study revealed that dual-wavelength LED phototherapy is safe and significantly reduces pain and discomfort in CEO, whereas topical antibiotics remain superior for otorrhea resolution. Collectively, LED phototherapy may serve as an adjunctive or alternative option, particularly for patients seeking non-antimicrobial treatment.

item.title: Needs Analysis of School Life and Therapeutic Support for Elementary Students With Cochlear Implants
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Although CIs restore hearing in children, comprehensive support is essential. Tailored educational interventions that address each child's unique needs are critical. Further research is warranted to explore long-term outcomes as students transition to higher education or the workforce.

item.title: Recurrence of neuromuscular blockade after sugammadex reversal of rocuronium: mechanism, stoichiometry, high-risk populations, and dosing evidence
item.description: Sugammadex is increasingly used as the primary antagonist for rocuronium-induced neuromuscular blockade and has reduced, but not eliminated, residual paralysis. A small but continuing series of reports describes a different failure: adequate recovery of the train-of-four ratio followed by a secondary decline in neuromuscular function, sometimes more than an hour later and occasionally after a recommended dose. Sugammadex encapsulates rocuronium in a 1-to-1 ratio, and binding occurs only in...

item.title: A UBE3A-UTX Proteostasis-Epigenetic Axis Governs Hypothalamic Energy Homeostasis
item.description: Energy homeostasis requires integration of metabolic and stress signals within hypothalamic circuits, yet the role of neuronal proteostasis remains unclear. Ubiquitin protein ligase E3A (UBE3A) regulates the stability of lysine demethylase 6A (KDM6A), also known as ubiquitously transcribed tetratricopeptide repeat containing, X chromosome (UTX). Hypothalamic neuronal deletion of Ube3a results in hyperphagia, obesity, hyperleptinemia, and impaired glucose homeostasis under high-fat diet...

item.title: Operative Treatment of Quadrimalleolar and Quadrimalleolar-Equivalent Ankle Fractures: Radiographic and Clinical Outcomes Following Component-Based Operative Fixation
item.description: CONCLUSION: A component-based operative treatment strategy was safe and associated with maintained anatomic distal tibiofibular alignment and favorable short-term outcomes in both QM and QME. The absence of a control group precludes conclusions on clinical necessity or superiority, and combined evaluation of these biomechanically distinct patterns should be interpreted with caution.

item.title: Treatment of Small Peri-Implant Buccal Dehiscence Defects With SCTG or GBR: 3-Year Results of a Pilot Study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Within the limitations of this pilot study, both SCTG and GBR were associated with stable buccal contour conditions and favorable peri-implant health over a 3-year follow-up period. These findings were observed under adequate self-performed plaque control and adherence to supportive care. Adequately powered RCTs are needed to confirm these findings.

item.title: Relationships among morphological variables, cardiovascular fitness during exercise, and thermo-physiological responses under passive heat stress according to Sasang typology
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: These results indicated that the Sasang constitutional types correspond to cardiovascular fitness level during exercise rather than thermo-physiological responses during the passive heat stress. Notably, the Sasang constitutional types were primarily reflected in morphological characteristics, rather than in thermo-physiological responses under passive heat stress. Further studies with a sufficient number of subjects including TY individuals during both heat and cold stress tests...

item.title: Circulating sphingomyelins and mortality in a community-based Korean cohort: the Korean Genome and epidemiology study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In this community-based Korean cohort, circulating SMs were not significantly associated with mortality or cardiovascular outcomes. This suggests that the prognostic relevance of circulating SMs may be limited and may vary according to population characteristics.

item.title: Effect of armed conflict on measles surveillance and zero-dose vaccination status in Tigray, Ethiopia, 2018-2024
item.description: CONCLUSION: The conflict was associated with a near-complete collapse of measles surveillance, marked changes in the age distribution of reported cases, and an increased proportion of zero-dose measles cases. These findings highlight the need for resilient surveillance systems and targeted catch-up vaccination during post-conflict recovery.

item.title: Integrated host-microbe biomarkers for early diagnostic classification of paediatric LRTI in mechanically ventilated children
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Integrating airway microbial profiles with host-response biomarkers supports earlier and more specific LRTI diagnostic classification in ventilated children. The seven-gene panel and cytokine combinations are candidates for rapid PCR- or immunoassay-based bedside tests to inform antimicrobial stewardship.

item.title: Development, implementation, and evaluation of a belief-targeted non-face-to-face leisure-time physical activity promotion program for South Korean University students
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Although the intervention produced changes in selected belief components among the total analytic sample, these changes did not translate into significant improvements in intention or behavior. Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested potential changes in control beliefs among participants with higher intervention adherence. These findings provide preliminary insights into the development, implementation, and evaluation of belief-targeted NFTF-LTPA promotion programs for university...

item.title: Exploratory associations between CT-derived body composition and MRI-based infrapatellar fat pad profiles with age-stratified analyses: a retrospective cross-sectional study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory retrospective cross-sectional study, CT-derived body composition metrics were not significantly associated with quantitative MRI-based IPFP profiles in the overall cohort, and interaction analyses did not confirm significant effect modification by age or sex. Although L3-based total fat area showed an association with Norm-P in the older subgroup, this finding should be interpreted cautiously and requires validation in larger prospective cohorts.

item.title: Patient and alignment factors associated with the occurrence and subtype differentiation of degenerative medial meniscus tears: a weighted comparative analysis
item.description: CONCLUSION: Higher BMI was independently associated with the occurrence of degenerative MM tears. In particular, both elevated BMI and HKA angle were independent predictors of MMPRTs, whereas no independent predictors were identified for MMHTs.

item.title: Living alone, socioeconomic status, and mortality among older adults: a population-based cohort study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: We found that although living alone is associated with mortality, adjustment for social and functional factors may attenuate this association. However, specific subgroups with low income, and scarce social relation lead to increased CCV mortality. Further study with a larger sample size is necessary to confirm this finding.

item.title: Human embryonic stem cell-derived mesenchymal stem cells ameliorate mitochondrial oxidative dysfunction in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease
item.description: CONCLUSION: ESC-MSCs ameliorated hepatic steatosis in MASLD models by restoring mitochondrial activity and reducing oxidative stress, possibly involving HGF-associated AMPK pathway modulation. These findings support the potential of ESC-MSC therapy for MASLD.

item.title: Surface Structure, Thermal Behavior, and Electrochemical Stability of Oligo(ethylene glycol)-Terminated Alkanethiolate Self-Assembled Monolayers on Au(111)
item.description: To investigate the effects of oligo(ethylene glycol) (OEG) chain length and thermal factors on the formation of self-assembled monolayers (SAMs), the surface structure, adsorption state, and electrochemical stability of SAMs of 2-[2-(2-methoxyethoxy)ethoxy]ethanethiol (EG3 SAMs) on Au(111) at an elevated temperature were examined using scanning tunneling microscopy (STM), x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and cyclic voltammetry (CV). To gain a clearer understanding, the results for EG3...

item.title: AI-enhanced hemodynamic prediction of patent ductus arteriosus severity in premature infants
item.description: CONCLUSION: The AI-based Extra Trees model demonstrated a robust ability to predict the hemodynamic status of PDA in VLBW infants. Thus, it may help NICU clinicians optimize conservative management and improve clinical decision-making.

item.title: The SCHENGEN pathway regulates lignin barrier formation via the receptor-like cytoplasmic kinase BIK1 in plant immunity
item.description: Lignin deposition is a hallmark of plant immunity, forming a physical barrier that restricts pathogen spread and confines hypersensitive cell death. However, how immune signalling triggers this barrier remains unclear. Here we show that in Arabidopsis thaliana, the SGN3 (also referred to as GSO1) receptor kinase and CIF peptides, known for their roles in Casparian strip surveillance in the root endodermis, also function in leaves during effector-triggered immunity to control lignin barrier...

item.title: A clinical multimodal vision language foundation model with fine-grain explainability
item.description: Despite their considerable promise, many current medical foundation models remain modality specific and lack transparent reasoning, limiting clinical adoption. To address this gap, we introduce Explainable Vision Language Foundation Model for Medicine (EVLF-FM), a multimodal vision language foundation model that combines broad diagnostic capabilities with fine-grained explainability. The development and testing of EVLF-FM encompassed more than 1.3 million total samples from 18 global datasets...

item.title: Multi-Stage buck strategy for power management of triboelectric nanogenerators
item.description: Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) offer transformative potential for self-powered systems, yet their real-world applicability faces a key bottleneck as their performance and efficiency suffer dramatic degradation below 5 V that the operational threshold for most electronics when integrated with conventional power management circuits. Here, we overcome this limitation through the multi-stage buck strategy that synergistically combines dual-stage voltage conversion circuit with TENG's output...

item.title: Intermediate-Phase Blocking as a Kinetic Lever for High Ionic Conductivity of Wet-Synthesized Cl-Rich Li Argyrodite for All-Solid-State Batteries
item.description: Achieving high ionic conductivity of wet-synthesized sulfide solid electrolytes remains a critical challenge for enabling scalable all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs). In Cl-rich Li-argyrodites, Li^(+) transport is strongly governed by the Cl occupancy at the 4d Wyckoff site, yet conventional wet syntheses fail to control this local structure due to the spontaneous formation of unfavorable intermediate phases. Here, we uncover that the formation of the PS(3)Cl^(2-) moiety during intermediate...

item.title: Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid cellular fractions reflect individual histopathological features in interstitial pneumonia
item.description: Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) cellular analysis is an adjunctive diagnostic tool in interstitial pneumonia (IP), yet its relationship with individual histopathological features remains unclear. We retrospectively compared BALF cellular fractions with 24 histopathological features in 67 IP patients who underwent BALF and surgical lung biopsy at a single center (2005-2020). False discovery rate correction was applied (q < 0.05), followed by multivariable logistic regression and Kaplan-Meier...

item.title: Correction: Exploring the association between adolescent psychotic-like experiences and components of social performance using a multi-level virtual reality paradigm
item.description: No abstract

item.title: Progestogens Modulate the Metabolic but Not the Musculoskeletal Response to Estradiol in a Mouse Model of Adolescent Gender Transition
item.description: Gender-affirming hormone therapy in transgender girls typically consists of gonadotropin-releasing hormone analog (GnRHa)-mediated puberty suppression followed by estradiol (E2) treatment. While the skeletal effects of this approach have been investigated, its impact on skeletal muscle and metabolism remains unclear. Moreover, the addition of a progestogen such as natural progesterone (P4) or synthetic medroxyprogesterone acetate (MPA) to the standard E2 regimen has gained popularity due to...

item.title: Robust continuous-flow oxidation of aryl-alkyl sulfides to sulfoxides and sulfones over titanium silicalite-1 using diluted hydrogen peroxide
item.description: A continuous-flow oxidation of sulfides was developed using a titanium silicalite-1 (TS-1) catalyst packed in a silica gel column and a single-phase MeCN solution containing diluted aqueous hydrogen peroxide (H(2)O(2) aq.). Methyl phenyl sulfide afforded methyl phenyl sulfoxide in 91% yield at a residence time of 6.5 min (flow rate: 0.20 mL min^(-1)), whereas increasing the H(2)O(2) loading and reaction temperature afforded methyl phenyl sulfone in 99% yield at the same residence time and flow...

item.title: Catalytic Substrate- and Site-Selective Transesterification
item.description: Substrate- and site-selective esterification is a powerful synthetic tool to reduce the number of steps required for the synthesis of complex molecules. To address the challenges associated with achieving such selectivity, a variety of strategies have been developed. However, these methods generally require highly reactive acylating reagents. We have developed the first catalytic process for a substrate- and site-selective transesterification using nonactivated esters as acylating reagents. The...

item.title: Biologie
item.description: No abstract

item.title: Targeting Mitochondrial Redox Signaling Promotes Neuroregeneration and Functional Recovery in a Multiple Sclerosis Model
item.description: Neurodegenerative diseases, including multiple sclerosis (MS), are characterized by progressive neuronal loss and limited regenerative capacity. To stimulate in vivo neurogenesis and oligodendrogenesis by harnessing the untapped regenerative potential of endogenous neural progenitor cells (NPCs) that are upregulated in the CNS under disease conditions, we developed a novel compound that targets Notch signaling, a pathway known to suppress neuronal differentiation of NPCs. Furapyrrodole, which...

item.title: The Probe Leads the Scalpel-A New Dimension to Gynaecology Care
item.description: No abstract

item.title: Teres Minor Fatty Degeneration Progression by Magnetic Resonance Imaging Analysis Is Associated With Graft Failure After Arthroscopic Superior Capsule Reconstruction
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This study showed that moderate-to-severe fatty degeneration of the teres minor and a smaller preoperative acromiohumeral distance are significant risk factors for graft failure after arthroscopic superior capsule reconstruction in shoulders with an intact or reparable subscapularis tendon.

item.title: Is HPC for you? A collective perspective on adopting high-performance computing for bioimage analysis in imaging facilities
item.description: Biomedical sciences use various imaging technologies and bioimage analysis has become data-intensive, often requiring resources that exceed those available on personal laptop computers or workstations. High-performance computing (HPC) can solve most of the problems connected to the data burden of modern bioimaging, offering scalable and reliable computational resources. However, most of the biomedical researchers and core facility staff might lack the required expertise and knowledge to fully...

item.title: Associations Between Patients' Perceptions of Physiotherapist Communication and Psychological Responses in Frozen Shoulder: A Multicentre Cross-Sectional Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Patients' perceptions of clinician-delivered information were associated with recovery expectations and selected catastrophizing-related thoughts in individuals with FS. Emotional state showed less consistent associations, suggesting that additional factors may contribute to emotional responses. Given the cross-sectional design, causal inferences cannot be drawn, and longitudinal and interventional studies are warranted to clarify the prognostic significance, and potential clinical...

item.title: Starch-concentration-controlled growth of anisotropic bismuth nanoplates: a facile and bio-assisted aqueous route to morphology-tuned optical response
item.description: Herein, we report a bio-assisted aqueous synthesis of single-crystalline, anisotropic bismuth (Bi⁰) nanoplates using starch as a dual reductant/kinetic regulator and poly(vinylpyrrolidone) (PVP) as a facet-selective capping agent. Powder XRD confirms the formation of rhombohedral elemental bismuth (JCPDS Card No. 44-1246) with no detectable crystalline impurity phases. Systematic evaluation of synthesis parameters reveals a surface-energy-driven growth mechanism governed by a kinetic and capping...

item.title: Prevalence and mortality of chronic extracellular matrix dysregulated diseases: a nationwide register-based study
item.description: BACKGROUND: Extracellular matrix (ECM) dysregulation, manifesting as fibrosis or tissue destruction, is a hallmark of many chronic diseases, leading to organ dysfunction and mortality. However, ECM-related diseases are rarely considered as a unified group, and their burden remains poorly defined. We aimed to quantify the burden of ECM-related diseases by estimating prevalence and mortality.

item.title: Interfacial Polarization and Charge Transfer in Al<sub>13</sub> Superatom-Organic Interfaces: Role of Frontier Orbital Overlap
item.description: Superatoms (SAs) have emerged as atomically precise building blocks for functional materials; however, their interfacial electronic interactions with organic substrates remain poorly understood, particularly in the absence of ligand protection. While most reported SAs are stabilized by ligands, ligand-free SAs provide a unique platform to probe intrinsic interfacial behavior. In particular, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) core-level shifts at SA-organic interfaces are interpreted as...

item.title: A seamless workflow for STXM-NEXAFS data analysis using napari: implementation of an ROI spectrum extraction function
item.description: Scanning transmission soft X-ray microscopy (STXM), combined with near-edge X-ray absorption fine structure (NEXAFS), enables the mapping of elemental distributions and chemical properties at a spatial resolution of tens of nanometers. A common approach for analyzing STXM data is to compare NEXAFS spectra obtained from regions of interest (ROIs). However, ROI-based spectral comparison typically requires frequent switching among multiple software applications. ROI spectrum extraction, spectrum...

item.title: Toward Chemoselective Modification of Selenocysteine-Containing Biomolecules Via Doubly Activated Cyclopropanes
item.description: Selective modification of selenocysteine (Sec) remains challenging due to competing thiol reactivity. In this study, we demonstrate that doubly activated cyclopropanes can serve as effective electrophilic warheads for Sec-selective modification. The electrophile undergoes efficient ring-opening reactions with selenols, while showing limited reactivity toward thiols. Selective labeling using Sec-containing peptides was confirmed by mass spectrometry. A biotinylated probe enabled protein-level...

item.title: Trinor-Guaiane-Type Sesquiterpenes with Unusual Skeletons from the Okinawan Soft Coral Clavularia viridis
item.description: Four new trinor-guaiane sesquiterpenes, clavuridin C (1), clavuridin D (2), 5-methoxyclavuridin B (3), and 5-epi-clavuridin B (4), together with three known compounds, clavuridin B (6), clavularin A (7), and clavularin B (8), were isolated from the soft coral Clavularia viridis collected from the coast of Cape Kyan, Okinawa Prefecture, Japan. The structures of the newly isolated compounds 1-4, including their relative configurations, were elucidated through detailed analysis of spectroscopic...

item.title: pdb2reaction: End-to-End Reaction-Path Elucidation from PDB Structures Using Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials
item.description: Elucidating enzymatic reaction mechanisms requires a sequence of computational tasks comprising active-site extraction, minimum-energy-path search, transition-state (TS) refinement, intrinsic reaction coordinate (IRC) validation, and quasi-rigid-rotor harmonic-oscillator (QRRHO) thermochemistrystages typically connected by ad hoc scripting and per-system tuning. We present pdb2reaction, an open-source Python command-line toolkit that automates this entire pipeline directly from a user-curated...

item.title: Precise Sequence Control and Thermal Characterization of N‑Substituted Maleimide Copolymers Containing Hydrazine Structure
item.description: N-Substituted maleimides are highly reactive and have been used for the synthesis of various thermoresistant polymer materials by radical copolymerization with vinyl monomers. In this study, we synthesized several maleimide monomers with N-amino substituents, i.e., N-(N',N'-dimethylamino)-maleimide, N-(N',N'-diphenylamino)-maleimide, and N-morpholinomaleimide, using N,N-disubstituted hydrazine compounds and maleic anhydride as the starting materials. We carried out radical copolymerization of...

item.title: Pinhole-Like Central Bronchial Narrowing: A Rare Reversible Manifestation of Eosinophilic Bronchial Inflammation
item.description: Recurrent atelectasis is occasionally encountered in clinical practice but may be attributed to repeated respiratory infections without thorough investigation, potentially delaying the diagnosis of the underlying cause. We report a 78-year-old woman with well-controlled asthma who developed recurrent right middle lobe and lingular atelectasis. Bronchoscopy revealed severe pinhole-like narrowing of multiple central bronchi. Although allergic bronchopulmonary mycosis and post-infectious...

item.title: Tackling the Growing Threat of Multidrug-Resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa in Sub-Saharan Africa: Challenges, Strategies, and the Way Forward
item.description: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a dangerous pathogen that has shown multidrug resistance in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) and has significantly impacted healthcare, where poor infection control and limited resources are common. This narrative review examines strategies in the SSA region to control this pathogen, reports its prevalence, highlights key challenges, and suggests future research. Studies published between 2010 and 2025 in PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar, focusing on AMR surveillance,...

item.title: Protocol for a phase I/II, open-label, single-arm trial of autologous chemically induced liver progenitor (CLiP) cell transplantation in patients with decompensated cirrhosis
item.description: CONCLUSION: This is, to our knowledge, the first clinical evaluation of autologous CLiP transplantation in patients with decompensated cirrhosis. The trial is designed to establish the safety and procedural feasibility of the entire therapeutic workflow, including tissue procurement, cell manufacturing, quality assurance, and portal venous administration. Efficacy-related observations are exploratory, and the lineage fate of transplanted CLiPs cannot be directly established in this study. The...

item.title: Lung Abscess and Empyema Caused by Panton-Valentine Leukocidin-Positive Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus ψUSA300 Strain in a Previously Healthy Adult
item.description: PVL-positive ψUSA300 CA-MRSA is increasingly identified in Japan and is primarily associated with skin and soft tissue infections; respiratory infections caused by this clone remain rare. We report a 49-year-old healthy woman with lung abscess and empyema caused by PVL-positive ψUSA300, successfully treated with vancomycin and linezolid. This case expands the known clinical spectrum of ψUSA300 and underscores the need for CA-MRSA consideration in otherwise healthy patients with severe pulmonary...

item.title: Probiotic toothpastes and mouthrinses: probiotic presence, viability, culturability, label accuracy, and effectiveness in vitro
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This study highlights that in contrast to probiotic lozenges, which are widely used for oral probiotic delivery, currently available probiotic toothpastes and mouthrinses may not consistently meet established probiotic criteria. These findings highlight the need to critically reassess their use in scientific research and the commercial use of the term probiotic, while recognizing that the present findings are specific to the product batches analysed and may not represent each brand...

item.title: The need for supportive policies: connecting individual placement and support to the domains of employment and mental health care
item.description: CONCLUSION: IPS can build a solid bridge between mental healthcare and employment when integrated into recovery-oriented services and supported by policies that promote inclusive, mentally healthy workplaces.

item.title: Association of CAF-Related Stromal Markers and IMP3 Expression With Lymph Node Metastasis in Early Colorectal Cancer
item.description: Accurate risk stratification for lymph node metastasis (LNM) is needed after endoscopic resection of early-stage colorectal cancer (CRC). We explored the associations of cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF)-related markers and insulin-like growth factor 2 mRNA-binding protein 3 (IMP3) expression with LNM. We analyzed data from 155 patients with pT1 CRC who were treated by primary or additional surgery after endoscopic resection. A matched case-control cohort comprising 18 patients with LNM and 29...

item.title: Convergent validity of the Functional Bridge Test and its prognostic association with walking independence in patients with acute stroke: a retrospective cohort study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The FBT demonstrated adequate convergent validity and prognostic association in patients with acute stroke. This practical bedside assessment was associated with early functional status and walking independence at a variable discharge-based endpoint. Further prospective validation using standardized follow-up time points is needed.

item.title: Outcomes of perioperative nursing practices performed by operating room nurses: a scoping review
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This scoping review descriptively synthesizes the outcomes used to evaluate perioperative nursing practices performed by operating room nurses across the perioperative phases. Diverse outcomes were reported across studies, reflecting the multifaceted nature of operating room nursing practice. Developing standardized, nursing-specific core outcome sets may improve consistency in future research and support evidence-based practice and education.

item.title: EGFR and TP53 mutations refine prognostic stratification of IDH-wildtype astrocytomas, not elsewhere classified
item.description: IDH-wildtype astrocytomas of histological grade 2 or 3 without the WHO 2021 molecular criteria for glioblastoma-TERT promoter mutation, EGFR amplification, or combined whole-chromosome 7 gain and 10 loss (+ 7/- 10)-are designated "Not Elsewhere Classified" (NEC), a residual category with clinical behavior ranging from indolent disease to courses clinically indistinguishable from glioblastoma (GBM). However, reliable molecular markers capable of resolving this heterogeneity have not been...

item.title: Association of medical visit frequency with cardiovascular events and mortality in patients with dyslipidaemia: a cohort study using a Japanese claims database
item.description: CONCLUSION: Less frequent visits were not associated with increased risks of cardiovascular events or mortality. Extending visit intervals may therefore be a reasonable option for selected stable patients receiving lipid-lowering therapy for primary prevention.

item.title: Immediate changes in trunk extension and pain following a structured exercise program in high school baseball players with extension-type low back pain: a retrospective observational study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: A five-exercise program was associated with immediate within-session improvements in trunk extension angle and relative pain intensity. The exploratory response patterns suggest heterogeneity in acute functional responses and may support individualized assessment. Given the retrospective design, no control group, fixed exercise order, and unvalidated relative pain scale, the findings should not be interpreted as treatment efficacy.

item.title: Region-specific hamstring activation and its dissociation from subjective contraction sensation during leg curl exercise at different hip flexion angles
item.description: CONCLUSION: The ST is preferentially activated during LC exercise. Hamstring activation is both region-specific and longitudinally compartmentalized, depending on muscle length as influenced by HFA. Because NRS was dissociated from T2 values, hamstring resistance training should not rely solely on perceived muscle contraction, but should instead consider objective muscle activation characteristics. However, since NRS and T2 values were not directly compared in the present study, further advanced...

item.title: Effects of daily intake of cacao polyphenols, alone or with milk protein, on skeletal muscle mass in community-dwelling older adults: an exploratory 16-week randomized, open-label, parallel-group trial
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Over 16 weeks, HC and HC+MILK showed statistically significant favorable changes in BIA-derived muscle-related indices compared with NI, without a clear incremental benefit of adding MILK. These findings suggest a potential benefit for maintaining BIA-estimated muscle mass under habitual activity conditions, although the clinical relevance remains uncertain because no intervention-specific functional benefit was detected and changes in exercise type and intensity were not assessed...

item.title: A mixed-methods comparison of participatory and deliberative citizen engagement methods
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Using both citizen panels and an in-depth interview engagement approach in a mixed-methods design broadens and deepens the evidence base, highlighting the need to align method choice with specific policy and research goals.

item.title: CT-based simulation of impingement-free mechanical hip motion after unilateral total hip arthroplasty
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Increasing neck length and lateral offset improved simulated impingement-free mechanical ROM after unilateral THA, whereas neck lengthening increased LLD. Femoral head enlargement also improved simulated mechanical ROM, but its effect was limited compared with those of neck length and stem offset. The contralateral healthy hip may provide contextual patient-specific information for interpreting simulated mechanical ROM in unilateral THA.

item.title: Prophylactic antibiotics for pancreaticoduodenectomy: study protocol for a multicenter randomized controlled trial comparing tazobactam/piperacillin versus ampicillin/sulbactam
item.description: BACKGROUND: Pancreaticoduodenectomy (PD) is associated with a high incidence of surgical site infection (SSI), reported in 20-40% of cases. In patients undergoing preoperative biliary drainage (PBD), the risk is further increased due to biliary contamination. Tazobactam/piperacillin (TAZ/PIPC) has been shown to reduce SSI compared with cephalosporins; however, no prospective trial has directly compared TAZ/PIPC with ampicillin/sulbactam (ABPC/SBT), which is widely used in pancreatic surgery....

item.title: Data-driven identification of modifiable risk factors for colorectal cancer in Palestine using machine learning methods
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: After excluding screening-related variables, ML models that relied on lifestyle, socioeconomic, and contextual predictors showed promising internal validation performance in classifying CRC among Palestinian adults. Hybrid feature-selection methods combined with Ensemble learning represent promising candidate pipelines for future validation. However, the findings remain exploratory and require external validation in larger, independent cohorts before clinical or public health...

item.title: The impact of menstruation-related symptoms on women's quality of life, work productivity, and economic burden: a structured narrative review
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This review highlights the multidimensional burden of menstruation-related disorders extending from physical symptoms to mental health and functional outcomes. The predominance of presenteeism suggested that conventional metrics based on absenteeism underestimate the true societal impact. The observed gap between symptom improvement and functional recovery underscored the need for integrated approaches that could address both clinical and psychosocial pathways.

item.title: CD44-targeted near-infrared photoimmunotherapy shows potent anti-tumor effects in an orthotopic lung cancer model
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: CD44-targeted NIR-PIT demonstrated potent antitumor activity in an orthotopic lung cancer model. These findings support the potential clinical translation of CD44-targeted NIR-PIT as a novel therapeutic strategy for lung cancer. Further studies are warranted to optimize clinically feasible light-delivery methods and establish the long-term safety of this approach.

item.title: Individualized statin associated type 2 diabetes risk estimation with a deep causal model
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Recorded statin exposure was consistently associated with higher incident T2D risk across three longitudinal cohorts. The framework supports assumption-explicit research risk estimation and hypothesis generation and requires external recalibration and prospective validation before clinical use.

item.title: Intravital FLIM Pharmacodynamic Imaging Using FRET Biosensors
item.description: When studying the effectiveness of targeted anti-tumor therapy, measuring in vivo protein activity within the cancer cells in real-time is vital. This however presents challenges as post-translational modifications or binding of cofactors, and their dynamics, cannot be captured at the single cell level with traditional methods. The work of the last two decades led to the development of a broad range of genetically encoded FLIM-FRET biosensors that can be used to study protein activity,...

item.title: Direct medical costs of breast cancer by subtype and stage in Korea: a patient-level retrospective cohort analysis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Breast cancer expenditures in South Korea are heavily front-loaded during the first year post-diagnosis, driven by intensive treatments. National healthcare programs should implement subtype-specific, reimbursement policy to address the future economic burden breast cancer.

item.title: Temporal proteomics maps concealed-stage remodeling and reveals early mitochondrial alteration as an intervention target in a model of PKP2-arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy
item.description: Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy is a heritable cardiac disorder commonly linked to alterations in desmosomal proteins. While desmosomal dysfunction is a recognized pathogenic mechanism, the early molecular remodeling that precedes clinical manifestations remains unclear. Here we used a mouse model with inducible cardiomyocyte-specific knockout of Pkp2 (encoding plakophilin-2) and performed time-resolved mass spectrometry-based proteomics to map disease progression from early PKP2 loss to...

item.title: Effects of motion and white matter hyperintensities on reference region based ¹⁸F-SynVesT-1 PET quantification in Alzheimer's disease and healthy volunteers
item.description: CONCLUSION: Data-driven motion correction during reconstruction reduced the impact of head movements and attenuation mismatches, improving image contrast and quantitative accuracy. SUVR(CER) was less sensitive to motion and WMH than SUVR(CSO), indicating greater robustness. When motion and WMH effects were controlled, SUVR(CSO) provided slightly better group differentiation than SUVR(CER). These findings suggest that CSO may be preferred for group comparisons in well-controlled datasets, while...

item.title: Two-year longitudinal changes in pressure-flow study parameters and prostate morphology after prostatic urethral lift
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Symptomatic improvement after PUL was sustained for 2 years. Urodynamic parameters demonstrated an early reduction in voiding pressure and calculated outlet resistance, although their longer-term changes should be interpreted cautiously. Prostate morphology also changed during follow-up, with increases in prostate and transition zone volumes between 6 and 24 months.

item.title: Methane oxidation in African lakes increases with phytoplankton and outweighs photosynthesis-driven oxic methane production
item.description: Lakes are large natural sources of methane (CH(4)), a potent greenhouse gas, resulting from the net balance of inputs from anaerobic and oxic methane production (OMP) and removal by methane oxidation (MOX). Here we investigate spatial patterns and causes of MOX variability in 79 African lakes. MOX is highest in the most productive lakes presumably due to methanotrophs attached to phytoplankton, as well as in lakes draining the wetlands of the Congo basin presumably due to inputs of methanotrophs...

item.title: Twin pregnancy
item.description: Twin pregnancies occur in ~12 per 1,000 pregnancies worldwide and are associated with substantially increased maternal, fetal and neonatal morbidity and mortality compared with singleton pregnancies. Although zygosity describes whether twins arise from one fertilized egg (monozygotic) or two fertilized ova (dizygotic), clinical risk is primarily determined by chorionicity (whether twins share a placenta) and amnionicity (whether twins share an amniotic sac). Accurate early determination of...

item.title: Publisher Correction: Extracellular-matrix mediated stresses spatially bias myoblast fusion and myotube growth

item.title: Quantitative changes in 3D contact predict changes in enhancer-promoter regulation upon cohesin depletion
item.description: Enhancers are drivers of gene regulation thought to act via 3D interactions with promoters. However, genome-wide cohesin depletion causes only limited changes in gene expression, despite widespread loss of contact domains, raising questions about how 3D contacts and cohesin influence enhancer function. item.title: The Inhibitory Effect of Naematelia aurantialba Mushroom (Basidiomycota) Polysaccharides on Zebrafish Ulcerative Colitis
item.description: Naematelia aurantialba is a medicinal fungus, which has many bioactivities such as antioxidant, hypoglycemic, lipid-lowering, immune regulation, anti-tumor, etc. Here, we characterized and analyzed the composition and molecular weight of polysaccharides from N. aurantialba, and their bioactivities against dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced ulcerative colitis (UC) in zebrafish and the underlying mechanisms. item.title: Chirality-Endowed Hydrogen-Bonding Network Enabling Long-Range Order and Enhanced Ionic Conductivity for Room-Temperature Chemiresistive CO2 Sensing
item.description: High-performance room-temperature CO2 sensors are essential for noninvasive clinical diagnostics, yet achieving high sensitivity in metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) remains challenging due to restricted ionic conduction. Building upon our previous expertise in guest-ion-source assembly, a strategy is proposed to enhance ionic conductivity by constructing long-range order and stable hydrogen-bonding (H-bonding) networks via chiral molecular incorporation. item.title: Visualizing complex-amplitude assembly in high-order harmonic generation from oriented polar molecules
item.description: Polarization-resolved high-order harmonic generation from oriented polar molecules encodes electron recollision from opposite molecular directions, yet the underlying interference is hidden in intensity spectra. item.title: Diode-pumped Yb:LLF laser with multi-watt SESAM mode locking and broad CW tuning
item.description: We demonstrate a diode-pumped Yb:LLF laser that combines multi-watt semiconductor saturable absorber mirror (SESAM) mode locking with record continuous-wave (CW) tuning. Using a compact cavity pumped by a single-emitter 10 W multimode diode at 960 nm, the laser provides up to 3.2 W CW output with a tuning range from 996 to 1073 nm and a slope efficiency of 42%. item.title: Fast eighth-order Padé schemes based on Chebyshev polynomials for the direct Zakharov-Shabat problem
item.description: In this work, we construct fast eighth-order Padé schemes for the direct Zakharov-Shabat scattering problem. The schemes are based on an eighth-order exponential integrator obtained from the Magnus expansion. A direct extension of the conventional fast representation to the eighth-order case leads to insufficiently accurate results in the considered tests.
